q: In brown fat of hibernating mammals, thermogenin lets H+ flow back into the matrix without passing through ATP synthase. What is the effect?
options: Electron transport stops, because the proton gradient becomes far too steep to pump against
ATP production increases, because protons re-enter the matrix much faster than before
Electron transport and O2 use stay high, but the energy is released as heat rather than ATP
O2 consumption falls to zero, because the cells no longer need to produce any ATP
explanation: Thermogenin (UCP1) uncouples electron transport from ATP synthesis. With the gradient continually dissipated, there is no 'back-pressure' on the pumps, so substrate oxidation and O2 use continue at a high rate while the gradient's energy is lost as heat. This non-shivering thermogenesis keeps hibernating mammals and newborn babies warm.
